skills.name: critical-review
skills.description: Use for structured, confidential critical evaluation of a paper, a manuscript draft, or a set of claims — claims-vs-evidence table, load-bearing assumptions, reproducibility red flags.

skills.name: experiment-design-matrix
skills.description: Use when planning experiments, ablations, or evaluation matrices before running anything — factors and levels, fair baselines, controls, metrics, seeds, and stopping criteria as a design doc.

skills.name: experiment-to-methods
skills.description: Use when writing or refreshing a Methods / Experiments section from logged runs, provenance, and result snapshots — Methods-grade receipts with no invented numbers.

skills.name: figure-pipeline
skills.description: Use when turning experiment outputs or project data into publication-quality figures wired into the manuscript and reopenable as interaction objects.

skills.name: hypothesis-design
skills.description: Use when sharpening a research idea into falsifiable hypotheses, pre-registering claims/metrics/stopping criteria in the project brief, or pressure-testing whether an idea is worth testing.

skills.name: intensive-reading-notes
skills.description: Use when reading library papers deeply (intensive reading) and turning them into structured, linked project notes or reading cards with page-level evidence.

skills.name: interaction-figures
skills.description: Use when presenting a result as a reopenable figure or plot in the RightArea panel — visual standards (palette, sizing, legibility on any theme), choosing between a static figure and a CSV plot, and update discipline.

skills.name: latex-tikz-graphics
skills.description: Use when drawing publication-quality TikZ/pgfplots figures — architecture and pipeline diagrams, commutative diagrams, function/schematic plots, and data line-plots rendered by LaTeX itself. Templates compile standalone into the project's figures folder.

skills.name: management-science-empirical
skills.description: Use for management-science and decision-science research — causal identification (DiD/IV/RDD/panel), behavioral experiment design, robustness batteries, regression tables, and theory models with verified comparative statics. Evidence here informs decisions; the standard is "a decision-maker may act on this".

skills.name: manuscript-preflight
skills.description: Use before submission, sharing, or tagging a manuscript release — compile, citation integrity, bibliography sync, figure paths, desk-reject and anonymization checks, and git hygiene as one pass/fail checklist.

skills.name: ml-research-protocol
skills.description: Use when running empirical machine-learning experiments — baseline and ablation discipline, multi-seed aggregation, reproducibility logging, and results you can trust, decide on, and defend. Wires the experiment island to statistical-rigor and the manuscript.

skills.name: prisma-systematic-review
skills.description: Use when conducting a systematic review or structured literature survey — protocol, PRISMA flow, screening log, and synthesis, wired to the project's literature tools.

skills.name: project-kickoff
skills.description: Use when starting a new research project or study in this workspace — set up the brief, seed cornerstone literature, plan phases, and scaffold the first experiment island.

skills.name: rebuttal-letter
skills.description: Use when responding to peer review — mapping every reviewer point to a manuscript change and drafting a point-by-point response / rebuttal letter.

skills.name: related-work-pipeline
skills.description: Use when drafting a Related Work / literature review section, synthesizing prior work into a cited narrative, or comparing methods across papers — from the project library plus external discovery.

skills.name: scientific-visualization
skills.description: Use when creating figures — for analysis, notes, or publication — chart selection, colorblind-safe palettes, a ready matplotlib style file, and a plotting template that outputs into the project's figures folder.

skills.name: skill-creator
skills.description: Use when the user wants to create, write, or author a new agent skill (SKILL.md), extend agent capabilities, or asks to make a skill, create a skill, or define a reusable workflow.

skills.name: statistical-rigor
skills.description: Use when choosing statistical tests, computing power or sample size, reporting effect sizes, correcting for multiple comparisons, or reviewing a results section for statistical validity.

skills.name: symbolic-math
skills.description: Use when deriving, checking, or simplifying symbolic mathematics — algebra, calculus, linear algebra, ODEs — with SymPy verification and LaTeX output that goes straight into the manuscript. Covers math, physics, engineering, and economics derivations.
